John Newman, a former Army intelligence analyst, wrote Oswald and the CIA to ask what the agency knew about Lee Harvey Oswald before November 1963. Its full subtitle promises the documented truth about the unknown relationship between the U.S. government and the alleged assassin.

Newman works from CIA files themselves, tracing the paper trail the agency built on Oswald over years. He shows when documents were created, who saw them, and where the record looks altered or delayed. The book avoids wild claims and rests on records, which is why serious researchers treat it as a cornerstone of the Kennedy literature.
